# LiveRegion

The two announcement channels the whole application shares, rendered once in the shell. Nothing calls it directly — code calls `announce()`, and this is where the message lands.

## Anatomy

Two visually hidden live regions, one polite and one assertive.

## Props

None.

## Variants

None.

## States

Silent, announcing.

## Tokens consumed

None — the component carries no styles of its own.

## Keyboard

Not interactive.

## ARIA

Two `aria-live` regions with `aria-atomic`, one at each priority. `assertive` interrupts and is for something the user must hear now — a failure, a lost connection; everything else is polite. Rendering them once and writing into them, rather than mounting a region per message, is what makes an announcement reliable.

## Accessibility acceptance criteria

- Reachable, operable and leavable by keyboard alone, with a focus indicator meeting 3:1 in both schemes.
- An accessible name for every control, and current state exposed programmatically.
- No meaning carried by colour alone.
- Legible and operable at a 360px viewport and at desktop width, and at 200% zoom.
- Interactive targets at least 44 × 44px on touch-capable viewports.
- Mounted exactly once, in the application shell. A second instance means announcements are heard twice or not at all.

## Reference correspondence

None. The reference has no live region of any kind, which is why nothing in it is ever announced.

## Recorded deviations

None.
